newsitem.title: UK: UK fraudbusters raid ex-MGAM fund manager's home.
newsitem.headline: UK fraudbusters raid ex-MGAM fund manager's home.

text.p: Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) said on Saturday it had raided the home of former Morgan Grenfell star fund manager Peter Young and begun an inquiry into his conduct, after irregularities surfaced in the funds he ran.

The SFO said it had searched Young's home in Amersham, to the west of London, on Friday evening in a joint raid with officers of the City of London police. The fraud office investigates and prosecutes major financial crimes in Britain.

An SFO spokeswoman told Reuters no one had been arrested but gave no further details of the raid. She said the investigation had been launched on September 26 after it was referred to the SFO by the Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (IMRO).
She said the aim of any SFO investigation at the beginning was to determine whether criminal offences had been committed.

Young could not be contacted by telephone but has said he is being made a scapegoat. His lawyers, Peters & Peters, were not immediately available for comment, although they have said there were no grounds for allegations of criminality.

Young, 38, was sacked last week on grounds of alleged gross misconduct following the discovery of irregularities in three Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) funds four weeks ago. Two of these were managed by Young, who joined Morgan Grenfell in 1992 and was voted fund manager of the year in 1995.

Trading in the funds, which had totalled 1.4 million pounds, was temporarily suspended but resumed three days later after a 180 million pound ($281 million) cash injection by Germany's Deutsche Bank, the funds' ultimate parent company.

Deutsche acted quickly to limit the damage to its own credibility, but redemptions from the funds reached nearly 300 million pounds after they resumed trading and worried investors took their money elsewehere. Deutsche subsequently said it would support the three funds for a minimum of three months

But reports of misvaluations of unlisted high-technology stocks and a web of companies set up by Young, apparently without his employer's knowledge, led to intense speculation about the future of some of his superiors and brought into question controls not only at MGAM, but across the industry.

Young's immediate boss Glyn Owen, MGAM's chief European investment officer, and Keith Percy, its chief executive, as well as Mike Wheatley, head of compliance, have all been named in newspaper reports as being likely to face criticism.

Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, the investment banking arm of Germany's Deutsche Bank, has already announced an overhaul of supervision at MGAM and on Saturday said it would continue its own dissection of the funds under scrutiny.

This has been going on since August 21, when the bank was contacted by investments watchdog IMRO about a separate probe. As a result of this it discovered problems in the European Growth Trust and two other investment funds and IMRO launched an investigation into these.

"There now appears to be sufficient evidence for a criminal investigation to begin. We will be continuing our internal investigation which is due to be completed by mid to late October. This will happen alongside the SFO," James Murray of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG) told Reuters. Murray said the SFO had not searched DMG offices.

DMG is itself expected to face penalties imposed by IMRO, when the regulator finishes its own investigation, although the results of this are unlikely to be known before the SFO has wrapped up its own inquiry into the affair.

A company called Russ Oil & Technology, which is registered in Luxembourg, has been widely reported to be at the heart of the investigation into Young's activities, although half a dozen other Luxembourg-registered firms have also been taken under Morgan Grenfell's control since the problems arose.

Young has had his assets frozen by an injunction obtained by Morgan Grenfell and the Royal Bank of Scotland, which was trustee on two of the funds under the spotlight. This also covered the assets of Russ Oil & Technology. ($1=.6405 Pound)
